rounds.text: Albert David Ltd trades at an attractive valuation across multiple metrics, including a P/E of 15.5x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 1.05x [E2], representing a steep discount to sector benchmarks where the P/E sits at 30.78x and P/B at 3.03x [E6, E7]. This undervaluation provides a substantial margin of safety of 32.6%, supported by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value estimate of Rs 1155 per share against a market price of ₹ 779 [E41, E42]. The company demonstrates exceptional recent fundamental acceleration, highlighted by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 20% and profit growth of 291% [E17, E18], alongside a sharp quarterly margin expansion to 12% in September 2026 from 3% a year prior [E28]. Furthermore, the balance sheet remains exceptionally strong with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.08x [E34], while a major drop in capital work-in-progress indicates that capex is largely completed and new capacity is ready to come online [E36]. Conceded: the company has experienced poor historical sales growth of 6.20% over the past five years [E57], a low 3-year median return on equity of 8% [E25], and negative free cash flow of Rs -36 Cr in March 2026 [E33].

Albert David Ltd suffers from severe, multi-year top-line stagnation, evidenced by a compounded sales growth rate of 0% over 10 years and -1% over 3 years [E14, E16]. Profitability metrics are equally troubling, with a 10-year median return on equity of 9% dropping to a median of 0% over the last year, alongside an actual ROE of -0.4% [E23, E26, E13]. Operating margins have also compressed, falling 4 percentage points in the TTM period down to 9% compared to 13% three years earlier [E27]. Most alarmingly, the business destroys cash: operating cash flow was negative Rs -8 Cr and free cash flow plummeted to Rs -36 Cr in March 2026, creating a stark divergence from reported accounting profits [E32, E33]. Shareholder returns reflect this underlying operational weakness, with compounded share price growth sitting at -5% over 3 years and -4% over 1 year, accompanied by a heavy historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -65.2% [E21, E22, E49]. Conceded: [E18] indicates that compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reached 291% alongside positive institutional money flow [E40].

Conceded: [E14, E16]. While historical top-line metrics show past stagnation, trailing data reveals an immediate inflection with 20% sales growth over the trailing twelve months and quarterly operating margins surging by 9 percentage points to 12% in September 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E17, E28]. Conceded: [E23, E26, E13, E27]. However, this operational turnaround is powering explosive bottom-line acceleration, highlighted by a staggering 291% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a rules-in-favor screen score of 68 out of 100 indicating a high-confidence BUY [E18, E59]. Conceded: [E32, E33]. The company operates with a pristine balance sheet carrying a minimal debt-to-equity ratio of 0.08x, and its sharply falling capital-work-in-progress indicates that major capex is completed and fresh capacity is coming online [E34, E36]. Finally, the market is mispricing this fundamental earnings explosion at a mere 15.47x P/E against a sector benchmark of 30.78x, backed by positive institutional money flow [E6, E40].

Conceded: [E17, E28]. However, the bull's reliance on trailing profit spikes [E18] masks severe fundamental decay, including a 10-year compounded sales growth of 0% [E14] and a 3-year contraction of -1% [E16]. The operational turnaround cited is entirely illusory when matched against the collapse in operating cash flow to minus Rs 8 Cr and free cash flow plunging to minus Rs 36 Cr in March 2026 [E32, E33], generating an alarming cash conversion ratio of 8.00x against reported profit [E31]. Furthermore, return metrics remain dismal despite the bull's optimism, with ROCE at a meager 0.8% [E12], ROE at -0.4% [E13], and a 3-year median ROE of just 8% [E25]. Conceded: [E34, E36]. Yet debt has simultaneously ticked upward to Rs 34 Cr in September 2026 [E35], while shareholders face persistent negative momentum reflected in a 1-year price return of -9.9% [E48] and a 3-year share price decline of -5% [E21]. Finally, the low valuation multiple of 15.47x P/E [E6] is fully justified by inconsistent operating margins [E29, E30] and decelerating earnings warnings flagged by the rules-based screen [E64].
